comparisons.peer_topic: Collateral-Dependent Loans and Credit Loss Estimation
comparisons.peer_summary: Corporate loans are collateral-dependent when the debtor faces financial difficulty and repayment is expected substantially from collateral; fair value less costs to sell is used to estimate expected credit losses for these loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup address the accounting treatment for collateral-dependent loans within their nonaccrual or credit loss frameworks. JPMorgan discloses that certain nonaccrual loans considered collateral-dependent are charged down to the lower of amortized cost or fair value less costs to sell, and notes that a negative allowance may result if collateral value improves. Citigroup defines collateral-dependent loans as those where repayment is expected substantially through the operation or sale of collateral, and similarly uses the fair value of collateral (less costs to sell) to estimate expected credit losses. Both firms utilize the fair value less costs to sell metric for collateral-dependent distressed assets.

sentences.text: In accordance with regulatory guidance, certain nonaccrual loans that are considered collateral-dependent have been charged down to the lower of amortized cost or the fair value of their underlying collateral less costs to sell.
If the value of the underlying collateral improves subsequent to charge down, the related allowance may be negative.

A financial asset is considered collateral-dependent when the debtor is experiencing financial difficulty and repayment is expected to be provided substantially through the operation or sale of the collateral.
For corporate loans that are collateral dependent, the fair value of collateral (less costs to sell, as applicable) is used to estimate expected credit losses.

comparisons.peer_summary: Approximately $2 billion of accrued interest receivable is included in Other assets, and uncollectible accrued interest reversals were not material for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Citigroup discuss the materiality of interest income recognition on nonperforming or uncollectible loan components, though on different specific line items. JPMorgan explicitly states that interest income on nonaccrual loans recognized on a cash basis was not material for 2024 and 2023. Citigroup discloses that amounts of accrued interest receivable considered uncollectible and reversed through interest income were not material for 2024 and 2023. While JPMorgan refers to cash-basis interest recognition on nonaccrual loans and Citigroup refers to reversals of uncollectible accrued interest, both disclosures highlight that interest-related adjustments for impaired credit conditions were not material, reflecting a similar conclusion regarding the immateriality of credit-related interest adjustments for the period.

comparisons.peer_topic: Nonaccrual Loan Metrics and Collateral Dependence
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 2024, nonaccrual loans included $322 million past due 30+ days, the allowance for loan losses was 127.8% of nonaccrual loans, and collateral-dependent loans rely on underlying collateral value for repayment.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose specific accounting and credit quality metrics for nonaccrual loans. JPMorgan states that generally all consumer nonaccrual loans have an allowance and that collateral-dependent loans are charged down to the lower of amortized cost or fair value less costs to sell, with interest income on a cash basis not being material. Similarly, Goldman Sachs reports that its allowance for loan losses as a percentage of total nonaccrual loans was 127.8%, and explicitly states that for collateral-dependent loans (such as commercial and residential real estate), the allowance is determined by considering the fair value of the collateral less estimated costs to sell. Both firms apply the lower-of-cost-or-collateral-fair-value principle to collateral-dependent nonaccrual assets.

sentences.text: (a)Generally, all consumer nonaccrual loans have an allowance.

In accordance with regulatory guidance, certain nonaccrual loans that are considered collateral-dependent have been charged down to the lower of amortized cost or the fair value of their underlying collateral less costs to sell.
(b)Interest income on nonaccrual loans recognized on a cash basis was not material for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023.
• Allowance for loan losses as a percentage of total nonaccrual loans was 127.8% as of December 2024 and 122.0% as of December 2023.

• Commercial real estate, residential real estate, securities-based and other collateralized loans are collateral dependent loans and the repayment of such loans is generally expected to be provided by the operation or sale of the underlying collateral. The allowance for credit losses for such nonaccrual loans is determined by considering the fair value of the collateral less estimated cost to sell, if applicable. See Note 4 for further information about fair value measurements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Wholesale loan ACL methodology for non-similar risk characteristics
comparisons.peer_summary: For wholesale loans that do not share similar risk characteristics, such as nonaccrual loans, the allowance is calculated using the present value of expected future cash flows, observable market price, or fair value of collateral less estimated costs to sell.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs describe the methodology for calculating allowances on collateral-dependent nonaccrual loans. JPMorgan specifies that collateral-dependent nonaccrual loans are charged down to the lower of amortized cost or fair value less costs to sell. Goldman Sachs explicitly lists nonaccrual loans as a category of wholesale loans that do not share similar risk characteristics, for which the allowance is calculated using the fair value of the collateral less estimated costs to sell if the loan is collateral dependent. This confirms that both firms apply the same collateral-fair-value-based measurement technique for nonperforming collateralized loans.

sentences.text: In accordance with regulatory guidance, certain nonaccrual loans that are considered collateral-dependent have been charged down to the lower of amortized cost or the fair value of their underlying collateral less costs to sell.

The allowance for loan losses for wholesale loans that do not share similar risk characteristics, such as nonaccrual loans, is calculated using the present value of expected future cash flows discounted at the loan's effective rate, the observable market price of the loan, or, in the case of collateral dependent loans, the fair value of the collateral less estimated costs to sell, if applicable.
